text.p: Lithuanian newspapers carried the following reports in their Monday editions. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy:

- In a joint statement released on Saturday, the three Baltic presidents have asked for clearer declarations on security and NATO membership after U.S. Defence Secretary William Perry said the Balts were not yet ready for NATO membership.
- A man suspected of involvement in the 1993 murder of Respublika journalist Vitas Lingys, Igor Temkin, has been handed over by German authorities to Lithuanian investigators.

- The whereabouts of businessman Vidmantas Bukauskas, kidnapped in the port city of Klaipeda, are unknown. The kidnappers demanded a $200,000 ransom. Bukauskas bought Lada cars in Britain and sold them in Russia.
- Experts predict a 1.9 million tonne potato harvest this year, which will fully meet the needs of the country.

- AN opinion poll by Baltijos Tyrimai showed that 65 percent of the population plan to take part in the October 20 elections. The poll was led by the opposition Homeland Union Party on 14.7 percent support, followed by the LDLP on 12 percent. They are followed by the Center Union on 10.5 percent, the Christian Democrats on 9.3 percent and the Womens Party on 5.9 percent.
President Algirdas Brazauskas, associated with the LDLP, is still more popular than Homeland Union leader Vytautas Landsbergis on 10.4 percent and 8.4 percent respectively.
